root_idea.summary: The root denotes drinking milk directly from an udder or breast, especially an infant's suckling.
root_idea.development: From literal suckling, the lexical family extends to nursing and wet-nursing, foster kinship established through nursing, descriptions of suckling animals, and several figurative uses associated with secretive or mean behavior.

senses.definition: To suckle; to drink milk from the breast, and in the Quranic nursing construction, to nurse a child.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quran occurrence is the imperfect form in the construction of mothers nursing their children. Classical sources record رَضَعَ and رَضِعَ as dialectally varying Form I citations.

senses.definition: To suckle or nurse a child; to provide a child with nursing.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively with the child as object and of a woman performing the nursing. The Quranic forms include perfect, imperfect, and imperative inflections; these are one lexical sense.

senses.definition: To seek or request a wet nurse for a child; to ask a woman to suckle the child.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction may treat the child as the object of the request, with the woman who will nurse understood as the requested agent.

senses.definition: A wet nurse; a woman who has a child to suckle.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the plural مَرَاضِعُ, used substantively for women who may nurse a child. The singular citation is normalized from the supported active-participial family.

senses.definition: A woman actively suckling a child.
senses.usage_conditions: This feminine active participle emphasizes the nursing action itself, especially the woman with the child's teat in her mouth, rather than merely the state of having a nursing child.

senses.definition: Suckling; breastfeeding or the period of nursing an infant.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for the act or completion of nursing, including the nursing period referred to in the Quranic family-law context.

senses.definition: Fosterage or foster kinship established through suckling.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for relationships and legal kinship created by nursing, including the corresponding marriage restrictions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be mean, sordid, or ignoble; meanness or sordidness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative development from secretly sucking an animal's teat rather than openly milking it; it may also be explained as having sucked meanness from one's mother's breast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a disputed reading, for milk to become scant, or to cause the milk of milch animals to diminish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied passage itself reports that the wording may be corrupt and proposes an alternative reading; the meaning is therefore lexical but textually uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suckle with another, or to have another suckle with one; to share nursing and thereby become foster-siblings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form III construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual sipping or drinking from a cup, especially a wine-cup.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use of the mutual-suckling construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An infant's nursing from its mother while she is pregnant with another child.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form III nursing construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give or deliver a son to a woman to nurse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction in which the child is entrusted to the woman who will suckle him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female having milk although she has no child currently being suckled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A possessive or descriptive use distinct from the active act of nursing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a reported usage, to cause a child to be suckled, possibly through a wife or female slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied source marks this interpretation as app., so the mediating nursing woman and the precise causative construction remain uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For two persons to suck the breast of one woman together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal Form VI construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a she-goat to drink or suck its own milk from its udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive Form VIII use applied to an animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Drinking from a cup, especially drinking wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative Form VIII use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of tree on which camels feed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct nominal use unrelated to the nursing action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The young shoots or suckers of palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun; the same entry also records a separate figurative sense of meanness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A foster-brother or foster-sibling by nursing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal relationship term derived from shared suckling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A suckling child, especially one not yet weaned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also be applied to a young animal described as still nursing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The west wind, or a wind between the west and south winds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized wind name, explained in relation to its effect on the milk of milch animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female animal that suckles its young, especially a ewe or she-goat with a nursing young one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine noun for the nursing animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stingy person who secretly sucks milk directly from an animal's teat instead of openly milking it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may describe a miserly owner or a herdsman who avoids carrying a milking vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beggar, one who begs gifts from people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use of the teat-sucking image.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who eats food particles remaining between his teeth so that nothing is lost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare figurative characterization of extreme parsimony.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A possessor of milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A possessive epithet formed in the manner of other nouns denoting possession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A milk tooth, especially a central incisor, or collectively the deciduous teeth of a child or young animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may include the teeth that grow and later fall out during the nursing period.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The breast as the place from which milk is suckled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural مَرَاضِعُ is formally identical with the Quranic plural presented under the wet-nurse entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of sucking the breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An infinitival use of the same nominal form, with plural مَرَاضِعُ reported in the supplied evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Suckled or nursed; a child still receiving nursing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Opposed to a weaned child.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who has a suckling child with her.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This possessive epithet describes the state of having a nursing child and need not assert that the woman is nursing at the precise moment of reference.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A position of command or governance together with the benefit or profit it brings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression contrasting the profitable office with death, the 'weaning' that ends its benefits.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A metaphorical epithet for bees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural metaphor based on the image of suckling or drinking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unborn child whose mother is nursing another child; such a fetus was described as meagre or poorly nourished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use concerning simultaneous pregnancy and nursing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A child or person for whom a wet nurse has been sought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may be understood with an elided phrase meaning 'one for whom a wet nurse has been sought.'

cautions: The Form I citation is normalized as رَضِعَ, while the supplied classical evidence also records رَضَعَ and differing vowel patterns as dialectal variants.

مَرَاضِعُ is formally ambiguous: it is also reported as the plural of مَرْضَعٌ, 'breast' or 'place of sucking.' The Quranic form is presented here under مُرْضِعٌ, 'wet nurse,' based on the supported participial reading and the supplied Quran context.
The milk-diminution branch is retained as a qualified classical meaning because the supplied Lane text itself questions the transmitted wording and proposes a correction.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Lane citation associated with مَرْضَعٌ is printed as 'xxviii. 11' in the supplied text and does not securely identify the QAC occurrence at 28:12:3; it was therefore not converted into a modern Quran location or used to force the breast/place meaning into the Quranic wet-nurse sense.
